                  <ns0:p n="25">25 To whom then will ye liken me <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">He repeateth what he said, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 18. that he might oblige them to the more serious and frequent consideration of the absurdity of the Idolatry.</ns0:note>, or shall I be equal? saith the holy One.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="26">26 Lift up your eyes on high <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">To the high and starry Heaven, as appears from the following words.</ns0:note>, and behold who, hath created these things <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Which you see on High, the Host of Heaven as it follows.</ns0:note>, that bringeth out <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">That at first brought them out of nothing, and from day to day brings them forth, making them to rise and set in their appointed and fixed times.</ns0:note> their host by number <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">As a General brings forth his Army into the Field, and there musters them.</ns0:note>, he <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 147. 4.</ns0:note> calleth them all by names <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">As a Master calleth all the Mem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bers of his Family.</ns0:note>, by the greatness of his might, for that he is strong in power <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Which work is a certain and evident proof of Gods infinite power<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:note>, not one faileth <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Either to appear when he calleth them; or to do<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> work to which he sends them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="27">27 Why sayst thou <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">In thy heart, why dost thou give way to such jealou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sies concerning thy God, of whose infinite Power and Wisdom, and Goodness, there are such evident demonstra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions given to all mankind, and to thee in a singular man<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ner?</ns0:note>, O Jacob, and speakest, O Israel, My way <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The course and condition of my Life. He takes no notice of my Prayers and Tears, and Sufferings for his Name, but suffers my Enemies to abuse me at their plea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sure, and doth not attempt to rescue me out of their hands. This complaint is uttered in the name of the People being prophetically supposed to be in Captivity.</ns0:note> is hid from the Lord, and my judgment <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Either 1. My Punishment: Or, rather 2. My Cause, as this word is most commonly used. God hath neglected to plead my Cause, and to give Judgment for me against mine enemies, as he hath formerly done.</ns0:note> is passed over from my God <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">God hath dismissed it, and left it and me in the hands of mine Enemies, and now our case is so desperate that God cannot help us: for which reason they compared themselves to dry Bones lying in the Grave, <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 37.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="28">28 Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the LORD, the crea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tor of the ends of the earth <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Of all the Earth and the inhabitants thereof, from one end to another. He seems to mention the <ns0:hi>ends</ns0:hi> or ut<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />most bounds, because they must seem to be more out of the reach and care of Gods providence, as being most re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mote from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> the only place of Gods solemn and publick Worship in the World, and being then thought to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>inhabited. The argument is clear and strong: God who made all, even the most desolate and barbarous parts of the Earth, and consequently takes care of them, will not neglect his own Land and People.</ns0:note> fainteth not, nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther is weary <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">He is not by age or hard labour become weak and unable to help his People, as men are apt to be.</ns0:note>? <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 147. 5.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>there is</ns0:hi> no searching of his understanding <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">His Counsels by which he governeth all the World, and in a most parti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cular manner thine affaires are far above the reach of thy understanding: and therefore thou dost ignorantly and foolishly in passing so rash a censure upon the Wayes and Works of the infinitely Wise God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="29">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:600" />29 He giveth power to the faint, and to <ns0:hi>them that have</ns0:hi> no might he encreaseth strength <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">He hath strength enough not onely for himself but for all, even the weakest of his creatures, whom he can ea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sily strengthen to bear all their burdens, and to vanquish all their oppressors.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="30">30 Even the youths <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The youngest and strongest men, left to themselves or without Gods help, or which do not wait upon God; which is easily understood from the opposition in the fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowing verse.</ns0:note> shall faint, and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="31">31 But they that wait upon the LORD <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">That rely upon him for strength to bear their bur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dens, and for deliverance from them in due time.</ns0:note>, shall <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> change.</ns0:note> renew their strength <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Shall grow stronger and stronger in Faith and Patience, and Fortitude, whereby they shall be more than Conquerors over all their Enemies and Adversities.</ns0:note>, they shall mount up with wings as eagles <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Which flyes most strongly and swiftly and high out of the reach of all dan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ger.</ns0:note>, they shall run and not be wea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> they shall walk and not faint <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">They shall be enabled to run or walk in their way as they please, without any weariness.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
